APPENDIX 
SCHEME FOR CASH AWARD TO JURNALISTS/PRESS 
PHOTOGRAPHERS FOR BEST CONTRIBUTION TO 

DEVELOPMENT JOURNALISM , GENERAL 

REPORT:NG AND News PHOTOGRAPHY 
1. The scheme shall be called the Kerala State 
scheme for Cash Award to journalists for best 
Development reporting (* ) General Reporting and 
Newsphotography , 

2. The scheme extends to the whole of the 
State of Kerala and covers all Malayalam Dailies and 
Weeklies published from the State. 

3. (a ) Th : awards will be given for each 
calendar year. 

(b ) The scheme will come into effect from 
1-1-1984 . 

4. The Government shall have the power to 
make any changes in the scheme or issue any clari 
fications in respect of the scheme wherever necessary . 

5. The decision of the Government on the 
awards under the scheme will be final. 

6. The Director of Public Relations will be in 
overall charge of the scheme and may issue necessary 
instructions in regard to its proper implementation 
from time to time. 

7. Journalists working in the Newspaper offices 
as Editor, Associate Editor, Assistant Editor , News 
Editor, Chief Sub Editor Senior Sub Editor , Sub Editors 
Staff Correipondents, Correspondents and Special 
Correspondents are eligible to apply for the awards for 
Development reporting and General reporting Staff 
photographers of Newspapers alone are eligible to 
apply for the award for Newsphotography. 

8. Correspondents establishments publishing 
newspapers and periodicals and readers of the general 
public may also bring to the attention of the 
Director of Public Relations articles/photographs 
which in their views deserve consideration for the 
a ward . 

• Development reporting is reporting the change 

that is taking place or ictended changes not 
taking place -in the lives of 

the people . 
Development reporting should tell the story 
of what is going well as well as what is going 
wrong. It includes reporting of non official 
initiatives in rural development, educational 
reforms, social welfare etc. and indepth 
reporting of official development programmes . 
All Development reporting is necessarily 
investigative.

Read :-G.O.Ms. No. 4 /83 /PR dated 23-4-1983 . 

In the G.O. read above sanction was accorded 
for the implementation of the scheme for Cash Award 
to journalists for best contribution to Development 
journalism . The judging committee constituted for 
selection of best Development report for 1983 had 
recommended in its report inter alia that the 
Government may also consider instituting of awards 
for General Reporting and news photography in 
addition to development journalism , and that 
reports published in Malayalam Wecklies may also 
be considered for Development Reporting.

9. The State Level awards will be Rs . 5,000 
for the best Development report, Rs. 3,000 for the 
best general report and Rs. 2,000 for the best News 
photograph and certificate of proficiency in their 
concerned field , 

10. (a ) Each year the Kerala Press Academy will 
constitute a panel of judges before the 31st January 
of the succeeding year to make recommendations to 
the Government for the awards. 
(b ) The 

Press Academy will evolve the 
procedure for fixing the awards, make the nomi 
nation , and communicate the 

to the 
Government. 

(c) The recommendations of the Judges for each 
year's awards should be submitted to the Govern 
ment before the 31st March of the succeeding year. 

11. Director of Public Relations will receive 
the applications before the 31st January of the 
succeeding year and forward the same after verifi 
cation to the Academy. 

12. No entrance fee will be levied . 

13. The Academy will have the power to decide 
not to give any award during a particular year .

NOTIFICATION 
C.S.R. NO..... In exercise of the piwwers conferred 
by section 8 of the Cinematograph Act 1952 (37 of 
1952), the Central Government hereby makes the 
following rules further to amend the Cinematograph 
(Certification ) Rules , 1983 , na uely: 
1. (1) These rules may be called the Cinemato 

graph (Certification ) ( Third Amendment) 

Rules , 1984. 
( 2 ) They shall co ne into force on the date 

of their publication in the oficial Gazette . 
2. In the Cinematograph (Certiication ) Rules, 

1983, in sub- rule (6 ) of rule 21, 
(a) in clause (b ), the word " and " occurring 

at the end shall be omitted ; 
(b ) in clause (c) for the words " court or 

authority " . the words " court or authority ; 

and " shall be substituted ; 
(c ) after clause ( c) the following clause shall 

be inserted , namely : 
" (d ) such film shall not be examined by 

the Board for certi6cation for public 
exhibition in India unless the Board 
is satisfied that the film is validly im 
ported in accordance with the import 
policy of the Government."

PUBLIC SERVICES SCHEDULED Caste / SCHEDULED TRIBE PERSONS 

APPOINTED ON PROVISIONAL BASIS THROUGH EMPLOYMENT 

EXCHANGES AND WERE IN SERVICE AS ON 2-8-1984— 
RETENTION IN SERVICE - CREATION OF SUPERNUMERARY 

Posts — ORDERS ISSUED 


GENERAL ADMINISTRATION (SERVICES - D ) DEPARTMENT 
9. O. Ms. No. 22 /85 /GAD . Datød , Trivandrum , 9th January 1985 . 


Read :-Government Circular Memorandum No. 73187 /SDI/84 /GAD 

dated 4-8-1984 . 


ORDER 
The Government have declared the year 1984-85 as the year of the 
Harijans . As a measure of Harijan uplift they directed in the Circular 
memorandum read above that the Scheduled Castes/ Scheduled Tribes 
employees who were in service as on 2-8-1984 on a provisional basis would 
be allowed to continue even if their term of 180 days expired , until further 
orders. It has also been specified in the circular that the orders would 
not be applicable to 

(i) those SC /ST employees who were appointed provisionally 
through Employment Exchanges under Rule 9 (a ) (1) of the 
General Rules to the posts reserved for SC /ST by special recruit 
ment on the basis of the instructions issued in Circular No. 
88342 / Ec . A2/83 /GAD dated 21-1-1984 ; and 

(ii) those SC /ST employees who might be appointed provisi 
onally through Employment Exchanges under Rule 9 (a ) (i) of the 

General Rules after 2-8-1994 . 
2. It has been brought to the notice of Government by several 
Heads of Departments that the services of some of 

the beneficiaries 
of the Circular Memorandum read above had to be terminated either 
due to 

want of vacancies or to accommodate regular recruits of the 
Public Service Commission . 

G. 109 


3 . Government have considered the matter and are pleased to order 
as follows: 

(i) The Scheduled Caste /Scheduled Tribe provisional employees 
eligible for continuance as per the circular memorandum read above, but 
had to be retrenched for want of vacancies will be reappointed in any 
available open vacancy in the department concerned . 

(ü ) The Heads of Departinents and Appointing Authorities will send 
proposals in the concerned Administrative Department in the Secretariat 
for creation of supernumerary posts where no open vacancies are available 
to reappoint the retrenched SC /ST provisional employees. Supernumerary 
posts will also be created in cases where retrenchment is inevitable when 
the nominees of the Public Service Commission report for duty against the 
vacancies reported to the Commission before the issue of the circular 
memorandum dated 4-8-1984 so as to accommodate the SC /ST persons 
until regular vacancies become available. 

( iii) The concerned Administrative Departments of the Secretariat 
will ensure that the proposals for creation of Supernumerary posts received 
by them are promptly attended to and necessary orders issued as quickly 
as possible. 

(iv ) The supernumerary posts , so created , will be adjusted against 
the arising fulure vacancies. 

By order of the Governor , 

M. DANDAPANI, 
Commissioner and Secretary

ORDER 


In the circular read above Government have ordered that in cases 
where candidates are undergoing any training or are in the midst of educa 
tional courses when they are advised by the Kerala Public Service 
Commission for appointment they will be given suitable extension of time 
to join duty so as to enable them to complete the course and that in all 
other cases extension of time for joining duty normally should not exceed 
three months at the most . 

2. The above orders are applicable only for appointment in 
Government Departments and are not applicable to appointments in 
Government Companies/ Boards or Corporations. The Secretary, Kerala 
Khadi and Village Industries Board "has therefore requested that the 
authority competent to 

grant extension of joining time in the case of 
candidates advised by the Kerala Public Service Commission for appoint 
ment in Government Companies/ Board/Corpora ions may be determined by 
the Government. 

3 . The Government have examined the matter and are pleased to 
prescribe the authorities mentioned below ' as the competent authorities for 
the grant of extension of joining time to the candidates recruited through 
Kerala Public Service Commission and appointed in Public Sector Under 
takings, Boards, Corporations etc. 

(i) The Chief Executives of the Public Sector Undertakings, 
Boards, Corporations etc. shall be the competent authority for the grand 
of extension of joining time not exceeding three months. 


206 


ü ) The Chief Executives with the prior approval of the Board 
of Directors shall be the competent authority for the grant of extension 
of joining time beyond a period of three months.

NOTIFICATION 


G.O. (MS) No. 4 /85 /Home . Dated , Trivandrum , 5th January 1983 , 
KERALA POLICE BANDS (PERFORMANCE AND FUNDS) 

RULES 1985 
Preamble :-In supersession of all earlier orders issued in the matter , 
the Government of Kerala hereby issue the following rules viz: 


PART 1 - GENERAL 
1 . Title and commencement. These Rules shall be called the Kerak 
Police Bands ( Performance and Funds) Rules, 1985 . 

(a) These rules shall be applicable to all the brass bands and Pipe 
bands in the Kerala Police . 

(b ) This shall come into force at once. 

2. Object. The object of the Police Bands fis primarily to attend to 
ceremonial functions of the Police department and to provide entertain 
ment to the personnel of the Units. 

PART II - PERFORMANCE OF BANDS 
3. (a ) The Bands may also perform as on duty at State functions 
like the Independence Day and Republic Day Parades, Guards of Honour, 
visits of the President of India and the Heads of Foreign Nations etc. 

(b ) The Bands may also perform at private functions on payment 
of charges and in accordance with the conditions specified in these rules. 

(c) The Director General and Inspector General of Police may 
order the performance of the Bands free of performance charges at spořte 
and games meets . 

4. The detailing of the Bands as provided for in sub rules (b ) and (c ) 
of rule 3 above will be subject to the following conditions. 

(a ) The Bands shall not attend functions arranged by Political or 
religious groups and their cover organisations. 

(b) The Bands shall not attend domestic functions like marriages. 
birth day parties, etc. 

G. 110 


(c) Notwithstanding anything provided for ekewhere in these 
rules , the Bands shall not attend functions, the status of which is not in 
keeping with the dignity and decorum of the police. 

(a ) A Band shall normally attend private functions only in the 
district where it has its headquarters or in the neighbouring districts. 

5. The Head of the Unit to which the Band belongs will be 
competent to order the attendance of the Band at private functions subject 
to sub -rule (L ) of Rule 3. above. 

6. (a ) The Bands shall travel only in conveyances provided by the 
Unit and shall not in any case , travel in conveyances arranged by private 
parties. 

(b) The Bands shall not accompany processions of any kind , 

(c) The duration of the performance by the Band at any function , 
subject to sub -rule (b) and (c) of Rule 3 , above shall not exceed thret hours 
within a period of 24 hours . 

7. (a). The charges payable by private parties for a performance 
subject to sub -rule (b ) of rule 3 by the Band will be as below : 

(1) A lumpsum charge for the performance . 
(2) Charge for transportation as per the rates of hire, charges 

for Government vehicles fixed by Government from time 

to time. 
(3) Travelling allowance for the personnel of the Band at the 

rates prescribed by the Government for other official 

kejourneys on tour. 
(b) For performances as provided for in sub- rule (c) of Rule 3, no 
lumpsum charge for performance will be levied , but the charge for trans 
portation and travelling allowances as prescribed in sub -rule (a ) above will 
to paid by the party at whose request the band is ordered to perform . 
73.8 . The lumpsum charge for performance mentioned in Rule 7 above 
3 ) will be as fixed by the Director General and Inspector General of Police 
from time to time. 

9. The charges as specified in rule 7 above and security deposit of 
Rs. 250 will be rcmitted by the party concerned in advance in cash or by 
demand draft drawn in favour of the Head of Unit to which the Band 
belongs. 

PART III - BAND FUND AND ITS OPERATIONS 
10. Each unit which has a Band shall have a fund called the Band 
Fund and this Fund will be a private fund of that unit. 

11. The charges levied as specified in rulc 7 above shall be disposed 
of as indicated below : 

(a ) The lumpsum charge for performance will be deposited in the 
Band Fund of the Unit . 


! 


( ) The charge for transportation will be remitted to Government 
under 055 Police (1) other receipts 2 Miscellancous" . 

(c ) The travelling allowance will be disburscd to the personnel of 
the Band . When travelling allowance is paid in this manner, the personnel 
of the Band will not be eligible for travelling allowances from Government 
funds. 

12. The charges levied as specified in rule 7 above and the security 
deposit will be immediately accounted for in the Band Fund and will 
thereafter be disposed of as specified in rulc 11 above . 

13 . The Head of the Unit shall administer the Fund . 

14 . The Officer Commanding of the HQ Coy in respect of the 
Battalions and the Cashier, Armed Reserve in respect of the Districts shall 
keep the cash and the accounts of the fund . 

15. The fund shall be operated through a Treasury Savings Bank 
account and the cash kept in hand shall not exceed Rs. 500. 

16. The fund may be utilised : 

(a ) For supplementing expenditure from Government for the 
procurement, maintenance and upkeep of the linstruments, equipment and 
ceremonial uniform of the Band , 

(b ) For special measures for the welfare of the personnel of the 
Bands, 

and 
(c ) For the payment of honorarium to the personnel of the Band at 
the rate of 50 % of the lump sum charges received in a financial year to be 
devided equally among the personnel of the Band , subject to a maximum 
of Rs. 360 per head per annum to be paid in the month of May . 

17. (a) The powers to sanction expenditure from the fund will be 
as specified below : 
Head of the Unit 

Upto Rs. 1,000 in one instance . 
Deputy Inspecior General Upto Rs. 5,000 in one instance . 

of Police of the Range 
Inspector General of Police & Amounts above Rs. 5,000 

Director General of 

Police , 

(b ) The Director General and Inspector General of Police may , by 
specific order , transfer specific amounts from the Band Fund to the Regi 
mental Fund in the case of Battalions and the Unit Amenity Fund in the 
case of Districts. 

18. All equipments , instruments and ecremonial uniforms of the 
Band will remain as Government propertics, irrespective of any expenditure 
that may be incurred from the fund for their procurement, maintenance 
and upkeep . 


PART IV - AUDIT 
19. The head of the Unit shall get the accounts of the Bank Fur 
audited once in every quarter, by a competent Auditor. 

By order of the Governor, 

N , KALEESWARAN , 
Commissioner and Secretary to Government . 


Explanatory Note 
( This does not form part of the notification , but is intended to indicate 
its general purport.) . 

There were separate orders governing the functioning of the various 
Bands in the Police Department. It has been decided that it is better to 
prescribe common rules and uniform 

for all Bands in the Police 
Department in supersession of all earlier orders, in the matter and hence the 
above notification .

For Union 


2 


AWARD 
The issue referred for adjudication by Government as per G. O. (Rt.) 
No. 469 /82 /LBR dated 29-4-1982 is the following : 

“ Wheter denial of employment to Shri B. Vijayan is proper and 

justified ? If not whether he is entitled to reinstatement or 

and any other relief ? " 
2. The allegations contained in the charter of demands raised by the 
Union , copy of which is appended to the reference, are as follows : 

Shri Vijayan was continuously working in the Kathayee Cotton Mills 
from 10th ofMarch 1978 till 9-6-1981 . He was an active worker of the 
Union and for that reason alone the management had denied him employ 
ment with effect from 9-6-1981 . He was earning a daily wages of Rs. 7.25 
and he is entitled to reinstatement with arrears in wages at that rate . The 
management has to be directed to give him those reliefs . 

3 . The contentions of the management in its written statement are as 
follows : 

The reference is not maintainable in law and on facts. Shri Vijayan was 
only a casual worker employed occasionally depending on the availability of 
work . He did not make himself available for work after 8-6-1981 and 
naturally he was not therefore employed . Shri Vijayan had not worked 240 
days or more in any of the years 1979 , 1980 and 1981. He had no permanency 
in the establishment as a worker . The Management has no liability to 
provide him with work . Further it has no objection to engage him as a 
casual worker whenever work is available as it used to be earlier . Shri 
Vijayan is not entitled to any other reliefs. 

4. In the rejoinder it is alleged that the denial of employment to 
Shri Vijayan amounts to a termination in violation of the provisions of 
Chapter V -A and V - B of the Industrial Disputes Act and the contentions 
raised by the Management are all false. 

4. The evidence available consists of the testimony of WW1, WW2 
MW1 and Exts. M1 and W1 to W3. 

6. The issue as referred is to be answered as such . It assumes that there 
was a denial and the question posted is as to whether the denial is valid or 
not. Of course there is the other aspect to whether Shri Vijayan is entitled 
to any reliefs in case the denial is unjustified . The additional contention 
zaised by the Union that there was a termination in violation of the appro 
priate provisions of the Industrial Disputes Act need not " therefore be consi 
dered . 

7. The main dispute as could be seen from the rival contentions is as 
to whether there was a danial or abandonment. The further question arises 
23 to whether Shri Vijayan was a permanent worker with continuous service 
or only a casual worker occasionally employed . All these aspects can be 
considered together in the circumstances of this case . 


- 


3 


3. What is stated by Shri Vijayan in his evidence as WW1 is that the 
practice adopted by this Management is to recruit a batch of about 30 per 
sons at a stretch as apprentices and to appoint them as casual workmen on 
the completion of probation . He states further that in his case he was taken 
as an apprentice in March 1978 and that he continued as an apprentice 
till October 1979 and then absorbed as a casual worker on a daily wages of 
Rs. 5. He states that the daily wages was subsequently enhanced to Rs. 7 . 
He goes on to say that there was a strike by casual workers in the Company 
which lasted for a month in 1981. When the strike was called off all the 
casual workers were taken back . But after a week 20 of them including him 
self were sent out . Some of them were reinstated on 8-6-1981. But he was 
not taken back . WW2 is the present Secretary of the Union espousing the 
cause of Shri Vijayan. He states that Shri Vijayan was denied employment 
on account of the fact that he had actively participated in the strike of the 
casual workers. MWI, the Production Manager of the Kathayee Cotton 
Mills , has given evidence that Shri Vijayan after the period of apprentice was 
a casual worker employed only occasionally and that the casualworkers had 
resorted to a strike in 1981 demanding enhancement in wages and that that 
strike was called off on a settlement agreeing to give enhanced wages to those 
who pass a trade test. It is also stated by this witness that Shri Vijayan 
did not turn up for work from June 1981 onwards and there was no denial of 
employment . 

9 . Ext . Wi, E.S.I. identity card , Ext. .W2 attendance card and 
Ext. W3 slip showing payment of bonus for the year 1980 are relied on by 
the Union to show that Shri Vijayan was a regular worker . But the evidence 
of the Management's witness is that E.S.I. benefits , bonus and attendance 
cards are available in the case of casual workers also . There is not much of 
a dispute on that aspect as it is admitted by Shri Vijayan and his witness 
WW2 that he (Shri Vijayan ) was engaged only as a casual worker. It is 
common case that there was a prolonged strike by the casual workers of the 
establishment in 1981. That strike admittedly was called off as per Ext. MI 
settlement. Clause 2 of Ext. Mi is to the following effect: 


“ Both parties have agreed to put the casual workmen for a trade 

test and the management has agreed to revise the wages of the 
casualworkmen and the samewill be paid to those persons 
who succeeds in the test. The payment will be made with 
retrospective effect i.e. from the date of their re- entry into the 
service after the strike. The trade test will be conducted and 

completed on or before 31st July 1981." 
It is common case that all the casual workers including Shri Vijayan 
joined duty consequent on the settlement. What happened subsequently is 
the matter that is in dispute. According to the Union Shri Vijayan was 
thereafter denied employment because he was actively participating in the 
strike. On the other hand the management's contention is that Shri Vijayan 
did not turn up for work and it is real case of abandonment. 


10. We have to scrutinise the evidence in further detail to see as 
to whether which of the two rival versions is true . wwi and WW2 in their 
evidence admitted that Shri Vijayan was not an office bearer or a lcader of 
the union . It is further admitted that persons who were holding office of 
the Union were not denied employment and thatthey are still continuing in 
service . There is nothing to show that Shri Vijayan had taken extra activities 
in the matter of strike for the Management to adopt a rigid attitude towards 
him . WW2, the Union Secretary , has stated categorically in the cross 
examination that the Management had absorbed all the casual workers who 
were prepared to accept Work and they were made permanent and that Shri 
Vijayan was one of those casual workers who left without accepting the offer 
to accept the work . Of course in re -examination he had said that Shri 
Vijayan had not abandoned the job . But the categorical statement made 
by WW2 in the cross-examination has to be given more importance and that 
agrees with the Management's case that Shri Vijayan left without accepting 
the offer of the Management to take up the job . It is also pertinent in this 
connection to notice that the Management had offered in its written state 
ment to absorb Shri Vijayan as a casual worker if he is prepared to accept 
the same. Shri Vijayan in his evidence as WW1 had admitted during the 
course of his cross examination that he has a job in another textile 
mill, viz . G. T. N. Textiles . So it is evident that Shri Vijayan had 
abandoned his employment in the management establishment and accepted 
an alternate job in another mill. So this is a case of abandonment and not 
denial . That being the position Shri Vijayan is not entitled to any reliefs . 

11. In the result an ward is passed holding that there was no denial of 
employment and that what actually happened was abandonment by Shri 
Vijayan . Shri Vijayan is not entitled to any reliefs. 
Ernakulam . 

N. SUKUMARAN , 
27-10-1984 . 

Presiding Officer .

S. GOPALAN ,

and Secretary to Government 

( Agriculture and Forests) . 

Explanatory Note 
( This does not form part of the Notification but is intened to indicaie 
its general purport.) 

As per G.O.RT. 2452 /74 /AD dated 15-11-1974 9 poʻts of Wild Life 
Assistants were created by Government in order to absorb the 9 Wild Life 
Guide Trainees selected under special employment scheme. The Wild Life 
Assistants have to perform duties similar to the duties of any other Forest 
Officer enforcing Forest Act and Wild Life ( P ) Act with particular reference 
to Wild Life . Therefore it is necessary to declare Wild Life Assistants as 
Forest Officers, vested with powers to carry out the duties and functions 
of Forest Officer's under the provision of the Kerala Forest Act and Rules 
and Wild Life (P ) Act, made thereunder. This Notification is intended to 
achieve the above object .

RULES 

C. S. No. 435/84 
1. Short title and Commencement .-- 1). These rules away be called the 
Kerala Service ( Amendment) Rules 1984. 

(ü ) . They shall come into force at orice . 
2. Amendment of the rules.... In Part I of Kerala Service Rules : 

(i) in clause (b ) of rule 145 the word ' earned occurring in the 
second sentence shall be omitted , 

( ii ) for rule 146 , the following rule shall be substitutca , namely . 

" 146 Recovery of pension contribution in respect of Government 
servants on deputation to foreiga service shall be at the rate of 15 per cent 
of the maximum of the scale of pay of the post from which deputation is 
Ranctioned . If the scale of pay is revised or the Government servant geta 
promotion in the parent department, the recovery shall be at the rate od 


15 per cent of the asximum of the revixed scale of pay of the scale of pay of 
the post to which the officer is promoted in the parent department, as the 
case may be 

The leave salary contribution shall be 10 per cent of the maximum of 
the scale of pay of the post of the deputationist in the parent department. 
If the scale of pay is revised or the Government Servant gets promotion in 
the parent department, the recovery shall be at 10 per cent of the maximum 
of the revised scale of pay or the scale of pay of the post to which the 
officer is promoted in the parent department, as the case may be . 

The combined rate of leave salary and pension contribution shall be 
25 per cent of the maximum of the scale of pay . 

Contribution shall be paid for the actual period of duty in the foreign 
service including all kinds of leave taken while on foreign service . Contri 
bution shall be paid for each calendar month or part thereof and no contri 
bution shall be paid for the periods of joining time"'; 

(ii) for rule 150, the following rule shall be substituted namely : 

« 150 Contribution for leave salary or pension , due in respect of an 
officer on foreign service, may be paid annually within fifteen days from 
the end of each calendar year or at the end of the foreign service, if the 
foreign service expires before the end of a calendar year and if the payment 
is not made within the said period , inte est must be paid to Government on 
the unpaid contribution , unless it is specifically remitted by Government, at 
the rate of two paise per day per Rs. 100 from the date of expiry of the 
period aforesaid upto the date on which the cor tribution is finally paid . 
The interest shall be paid by the officer or the foreign employer according 
as the contribution is paid by the former or the latter " 


By order of the Governor , 
N.-M.ABDUL KADOK , 

Joint Secretary 


Esplanatory Note 
( This dod not form part of the notification but is intended to indicate 
Ito general purport) . 

The aisting rate of pension and leave salary contribution in respect of 
officers on deputation to foreign service is one sixth (1/6 ) and one twelveth 
(1/12) of the Officer's pay, from time to time in the State - service. With 
a view to simplify the existing procedure it has been decided to revise the 
rate of pension and leave salary contribution with reference to the 
maximum of the scale of pay instead of actual pay and to fix the rates on 
peroentage basis . This amendment is intended to achieve the aforesaid 
bijotive .

NOTIFICATION 
S. R. O. No. 210 /65. - Ia exercise of the powers conferred by sub 
section (1) of section 2 of the Kerala Public Services Act, 1968 ( 19 of 
1968 ), read with soctiou 3 thereof, the Goverareat of Kerala hereby make 
the following Rules further to amend the Kerala Service Rula , namely: 


C.S. No. 1/85 . 
1 . Short title and Commerctiseal.- ( 1) There mules may be called the 
Kerala Service (Amendment) Rules , 1985 . 

(2 ) They shall come into force at once . 

2 . Angridment of the Rules. - Io Part Ill of the Kerala Service Rules, 
to sub rule .(a ) of rulc 25 , the following proviso shall be added , namely : 

“ Provided that the benefit under this sub -rule shall be available only 
to employees who are recruited when practising at the 

Bar to posts 
requiring law qualification and experience at the Bar" . 

By order of the Goverzor, 
JORXPHINE ANNE CLARANCE , 

Additional Secretary. 
G , 189 

[P. T. o . ) 


Explanatvey Noto 
( This is not part of the amendment, but is intended to indicato its 
general purport.) 

Consequent on the introduction of Government decision No. 2 
below Rule 25 (a ) , Part III, Kerala Service Rules, the benefit of reckon . 
inz Bar servire for pension conferred under the above rule was confined 
to officers who are recruited at the time when they are practising at 
the Bar and that ton to posts reqı iring law qualifications and experience 
at the Bar. This decision was challenged in the High Court of Kerala 
and the High Court of Kerala allowed the O.P. In the judgement 
the High Court pointed out that Rule 25 ( a ) is a statutory rule 
framed by Government and it cannot be varicd or amended by an 
executive decision . Accordingly orders were issued in the Government 
order read as second paper, lifting the restrictions contained in the 
Government decision No. 2 . This amendment is intended to give statutory 
validity to the Government decision issued in the Government order 
read as Ist paper above .

GOVERNMENT OF KERALA 
Taxes (B ) Department 

NOTIFICATION 


G. O. (MS) No. 9 /85 /TD . 

Dated , Trivandrum , 23rd January , 1985 . 
S. R. O. No. 214/85 . - In exercise of the powers conferred by section 
10 of the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963 (15 of 1963 ), the Government 
of Kerala , having considered it necessary in the public interest so to do , 
hereby make an exemption in respect of the tax payable under the said 
Act, on the sale of consumer articles and minor forest produces by Harijan / 
Girijan Co -operative Societies in the State for a period of one year from 
the date of this notification . 


By order of the Governor , 

P. JADAYUDAI MONY, 

Joint Secretary to Government. 

Explanatory Note 
( This does not form part of the notification , but is intended to indicato 
the general purport.) 

The Registrar of Co -operative Societies and the Director of Tribal 
Welfare have represented to Government that the Co -operative Societies 
exclusively for the benefit of scheduled castes and scheduled tribes were 
formed to uplift the economic structure of the Scheduled Castes and 
Scheduled Tribes . These Societies are now undertaking distribution of 
consumer articles and collection and marketing of minor forest produces to 
ensure fair wages to the members who are engaged in the collection works. 
If sales tax is levied upon the Harijan /Girijan Co-operative Societies, the 
viability of these societies will be affected . The Government consider that 
the exemption should be granted to Harijan /Girijan Co-operative Societies 
in the State from levy of Sales tax for a period of one year. This notificati .. 
on is intended to achieve the above object.

11. Appointing authority , probation etc. 

The appointing authority to the post of 
Divisional Accountant shall be the Finance Secretary 
to Government. 

A person appointed to the cadre of Divisional 
Accountant shall on the date on which he joins duty 
undergo practi :al training for a period of 18 months. 
On the successful completion of the training he shall 
be on probation for a period of one year on duty 
within a continuous period of two years . During the 
period of training a trainee shall be given training 
allowance as fixed by Government from time to time.

Departments Offices . Applications which are not in 
che prescribed form will be rejected .

കണം. കൂടാതെ ലേലംകൊളളുന്ന തുക കരുതൽവില 
നിശ്ചയിച്ചിട്ടുളളപക്ഷം അതിനേക്കാൾ കുറഞ്ഞിരിക്കു 

പ്പുളള അനന്തരാവകാശികൾ തങ്ങൾ 3 ' പേരും മാത്രമാ 

ണെന്നും അവകാശപ്പെട്ടുകൊണ്ട് കോഴിക്കോട് താലൂ 
മ്പാഴാ ലേലത്തിൽ പറയുന്ന വില വ്യക്തമായും കീൽ കച്ചേരി വില്ലേജിൽ ശ്രീമതി സുശീല മാധവൻ 
അപര്യാപ്തമായതിനാൽ അങ്ങനെചെയ്യുന്നത് ആശാസ്യ 

എന്നവരും മററ് 2 പേരും ചേർന്ന് ഒരു അനന്തരവകാശ 
മാണെന്നുവരുമ്പോഴോ ഏററവും കൂടിയ ലേലത്തുക സർട്ടിഫിക്കായി (ലീഗൻമഹർഷിപ്പ് സർട്ടിഫിക്കറ്ററു ) ന 
സ്വീകരിക്കുന്നതിന്,

NOTIFICATION 
UNDER SECTION 6 OF THE KERALA SURVEY 

AND BOUNDARIES ACT, 1961 
No. A2-769/84. 

18th January 1985 . 
Whereas the Government have directed the survey . 
of lands comprised in survey numbers noted below 
it is hereby notified under subsection (1) of section 6 of 
the Kerala Survey and Boundaries Act, 1961, that 
survey operation will be started in the village soon and 
the survey numbers of the village noted below will be 
demarcated and surveyed ; and that every person 
claiming to be interested in the registered lands situated 
within or adjoining the undermentioned lands is hereby 
invited to attend immediately either in person or by 
agent on the surveyor employed in the locality and also 
from time to time when called upon for the purpose 
of pointing out the boundaries and supplying informa 
ation in connection therewith . 

Under subsection ( 2 ) of section 6 of the said Act, 
this notification shall be held to be a valid notice to 
every person having any interest in the said lands. 

Under subsection (3) section 6 of the above said , 
Act, all the registered holders are hereby required : 
(a ) to clear within 15 days by cutting down or 

removing any trees, jungle, fences,standing 
crops or other material obstcuctions, the 
boundaries or other lines , the clearance 
of which may be necessary for the purposes 

of survey ; and 
(b ) to provide labour at such time and for such 

periods as may from time to time be 
required by furnishing flag holders and 

chainmen ; and 
(c) to provide suitable survey marks and other 

wise to give such assistance in the survey 
as may be demanded under the said Act or 

the rules made thereunder. 

If any person fails to comply with these 
requisitions under clauses (a) to ( c) mentioned above, 
the work will be got done by employing hired labour 
and the cost thereof will be recovered from the defau 
Iters as provided in the Act and rules made thereunder.

1961, that survey operation will be started in the

that every person claiming to be interested in the 
registered land 

situated within or adjoining the 
uadermentioned land is hereby invited to attend

surveyor employed in the locality and also from time 
to time when called upon for the purpose of pointing 
out the 

oundaries and supplying information in 
connection therewith . 

Under subsection (2 ) of section 6 of the said Act, 
this notification shall be held to be a valid notice to 
every person having any interest in the said land. 

Under subsection (3 ) or section 6 of the above 
said Act , all the registered holders are hereby 
required : 

( a) -to clear within 15 days by cutting down 

or removing any trees , jungle, fences, 
Standing crops or other material obstruc 

tions, the boundaries or other lines the 
. clearance of which may be necessary for 

the purposes of survey; and 
(b ) to provide Labour at such time and for 

such periods as may from time to time 
be required by furnishing flag holden 

and chainmen ; and .

otherwise to give such assistance in the 
survey as may be demanded under the 

said Act or the rules roade thereunder .

ആവശ്യമായിട്ടുള്ളതുമായ ഭൂമി കൈവശമാക്കുവാൻ 
സർക്കാർ ഉദ്ദേശിക്കുന്നുവെന്ന്. ഇതിനാൽ നോട്ടീസ 
നൽകിക്കൊളളുന്നു . പ്രസ്തുത 'ഭൂമിയിൽ അവകാശ 
ബന്ധമുളള എല്ലാപേരും നേരിട്ടോ " അധികൃത 
എജൻറുമൂലമോതാഴെപറയുന്നതീയതിയിലും സമയത്തും 
സ്ഥലത്തും ഹാജരാകുകയും ഭൂമിയിൽ അവരോരോ 
രുത്തർക്കുമുള്ള അവകാശബന്ധങ്ങളുടെ സ്വഭാവവും 
ഭൂമിയിൽ അങ്ങനെയുളള അവകാശമ ബന്ധങ്ങള 
സംബന്ധിച്ചിടത്തോളം നഷ്ടപരിഹാരത്തിന് അവ 
രുടെ തേർച്ചയുടെ തുകയും വിവരങ്ങളും 
8 -ാം വകുപ്പു പ്രകാരം എടുത്തിട്ടുളള അളവ് സം ബ 
ന്ധിച്ച് വല്ല ആക്ഷേപവുമുണ്ടെങ്കിൽ അതും കാണി 
ച്ചുകൊണ്ട് പ്രസ്താവിക്കുകയും അവരോ അവരുടെ 
ഏജൻറുമാരോ എഴുതി ഒപ്പിട്ട ഒരു പ്രതിക സമർപ്പി ക്കു

UNDER SECTION 6 OF THE KERALA SURVEY 

AND BOUNDARIES ACT , 196 
No. E5-3152183 

18tha Jayuary 1985 , 
Whereas the Government have directed the 
survey of lands comprised in survey numbers noted 
below it is hereby notified undee subsection (1) of 
section 6 of the Kerala Survey and Boundaries Act , 
1961 , that survey operation will be started in the 
village soon and the survey numbers of the village 
noted below will be demarcated and surveyed ; and 
that every person claiming to be interested in the 
registered lands situated within or adjoining the under 
mentioned lands is hereby invited to attend immedia 
tely either in person or by agent on the survey or 
employed in the locality and also from time to time, 
when called upon for the purpose of pointing out the 
boundaries and supplying information in connection 
therewith . 

Under subsection (2) of section 6 of the said Act , 
this notification shall be held to be a valid notice to 
every person having any interest in the said land . 

Under subsection ( 3) of section 6 of the said Act, 
all the registered holders are hereby required : 

(a) to clear within 15 days by cutting down or 

removing any trees, jungle, fences , 
standing crops or other material obstruc 
tions, the boundaries or other lines, the 
clearance of which may be necessary for 

the purposes of survey; and 
(b ) to provide labour at such timeand for 

such periods as may from time to time be 
required by furnishing flag holders and 

chainmen ; and 
(c) to provide, suitable survey marks and 

otherwise to give such assistance in survey 
as may be demanded under the said Act or 

the rules made thereunder . 
If any person fails to comply with these requisi 
tions under clauses (a ) to ( c ) mentioned above the 
work will be got done by employing hired labour and 
the cost there of will be recovered from the defaulters 
as provided in the Act and rules made thereunder .

No. TX3/4000 /84. 

1st February 1985 
Diploma Examination in Engineering/Technology /Commercial Practice /Costume Design and 
Dressmaking (First, Second and Final Year ) - (New Scheme) -First, Second and 
Final Year Diploma Examination in Polymer Technology (Old Scheme) and 

Certificate Examination in Textile Technology- May 1985 
It' is hereby notified that the following First, Second and Final Year Diploma Examinations in 
Engineering Technology /Commercial Practice /Costume Design and Dressmaking as per the New Scheme, First, 
Second and Final Year Polymer Technology (Old Scheme) and Certificate Examination in Textile Technology 
will commence during the month of May 1985. As per G.O. (Rt.) No.462/84 /H.Edn.dated 31-3-1984 candidates 
who have yet to pass any subject under Old Scheme (First, Second and Final Year ) are also eligible to write the 
corresponding subject under the_New Scheme. Details of Corresponding subjects are available with the 
Principals of Polytechnics. Time Table will be Published separately .

3. The Principals of Polytechnics and other Heads of Institutions will be the Chief Superintendents for 
the conduct of the Examination . All Principals of the Polytechnics and other Heads of Institutions should accept 
the Chief Superintendentship and they will not be exempted from this work on any account. 

Candidates who have undergone the prescribed course satisfactorily in any one of the recognised 
Polytechnics in this State and who have secured the prescribed minimum attendance i.e., 80 % and above are 
eligible to appear for the examination . However necessary condonation for the shortage in attendance can be 
obtained for valid reasons from the competent authority . 

5. Candidates who have passed the First Year Diploma Examination only are eligible to sit for the 
Final Year Diploma Examination (under New Scheme) . 

6. Candidates who have failed the subjects in the previous examination need appear only for the failed 
subjects in the subscquent examinations . Such candidates should register for the subsequent examination for 
all the subjects in which they have failed in the previous examination . 

7. Piece-meal registration will not be allowed . 

8. Principals of Polytechnics should verify whether the candidate have remitted fee for all subjects in 
which he/she has failed . If any candidate has submitted application for partial appearance, such applications need 
Dot be forwarded to this office.

10. The fee for the examination should be remitted into a Government Treasury/in the State Bank of 
Travancore under the head of Account " 077 F (a) 3-Examination fees" . 

11. Fees from the regular candidates ( candidates on the roll of the Institution ) may be collected by the 
Principals of the Polytechnic and remitted in the Treasury or State Bank of Travancore (separate remittance may 
be made for the late remittance with fine) in the name of the Principal and the original chalan receipt forwarded 
along with the nominal list of candidates . 

12. Private candidates will have to remit the examination fee in the name of the candidate theinselves in 
separate chalan and the original chalan receipt should be forwarded with the applications to the Principal 
of the Institution in which the candidate has undergone the course . 

13. On no account the examination fee be sent to this office in cash or cheque or money order or postal 
order or in any form other than those prescribed above. 

14. Amount of Examination fee once remitted will not be refunded or adjusted towards the fee for a 
subsequent Examination . The fee remitted prior to the date of this Notification will not be entertained . 

15. Last date for remittance of fees with or without fine and the last date for receipt of applicationg 
and nominal list in the Office of the Controller of Technical Examinations are fixed as follows: -- 
Last date for remittance of fee without fine 

21-2-1985 
Last date for remittance of fee with fine 

28-2-1985 
Last date of submission of application with original chalan to the 
Principals by the Private and Regular candidates 

1-3-1985 
Last date for the receipt of the applications and nominal list by the 
Controller of Technical Examinations, Trivandrum -8 - 

16-3-1985 
16. The dates of remittance noted above are the dates fixed for remittance of fee into the Treasury by 
the Principals of Institutions and by the Private candidates and not the date fixed for the payment of fec by 
regular candidates in the office of the Polytechnics. 

17. Applications relating to those candidates who have remitted fec after the last date,need not be 
forwarded to this office . 

18. The fees remitted after the last date either by the Principals or students will not be accepted . 
19. The Principals of Polytechnics should remit the fee on or before the due date positively. 

20. The rules now in force in regard to the realisation of Examination fee from Scheduled Caste, 
Scheduled Tribe and Educationally Backward Classes may be followed . The Principals of Polytechnics should 
get the amount reimbursed from the Harijan Welfare Department and remit into the Treasury under the head of 
account " 077 F. (a) -- 3 -- Examination fees" and forwarded the chalan receipt to this office. List of concession 
holders in branch -wise ( in duplicate copy) to be forwarded along with the A and B list. 

21. The form of application for admission to the Examination is annexed to the Notification . Candi 
dates may use typed or printed forms on Foolscap size paper. Manifold paper may not be used for this purpose . 
The applications should be countersigned by the Principals or the Head of Institutions in which the candidates 
had completed the course. " Private candidates need not forward their applications direct to this office" . They 
Are to forward the applications with the original chalan receipt so as to reach the Principals of the Institutions 
where they had undergone the course before the dates specified above. Principals may collect such applications 
and prepare a list in the prescribed form and forward the same to this office with the applications received 
from the candidates along with the nominal list and chalan receipt etc., of the regular candidates. 

22. The Principals of the Polytechnics will scrutinise the applications and see that the entries made 
therein by the candidates are correct and agree with the records of the Institution , 

23. Change of Centre for the Examination . - Change of Centre will not be allowed to any candidate 
except for the candidates transferred from one Institution to another with the consent of the concerned authority. 
Others should write the Examination through the Centre from where they had completed the prescribed course 
of studies. 

24 . Cancellation of Candidature for the Examination . - If a candidate desire to cancel his candidature for the 
Examination he/she should forward the application duly recommended by the Principal of the Polytechnic so 
as to reach the office of the Controller of Technical Examinations 3 days before the actual commencement of the 
first day of the Examination . If any candidate has appeared in any of the papers for the Examination his candi 
dature for the Examination will not be cancelled. Only candidates who have applied for cancellation of the 
Examination as stated above are eligible to get I class in the next appearance. Those who have applied for the 
Examination and absent without cancelling their appearance will be considered as appeared for the Examination 
and their subsequent appearance will be treated as Second chance. 

25. Issue of Mark List.– Mark list will be issued to the candidates through the Principals of the Examin 
ation Centre . 

26 . Practical Examination. - Candidates will not be permitted to take their practical test in any 
Polytechnic other than the Institution in which they had undergone the Course. 
,f . 30/J.

27 . Candidates should contact the Principal (Chief Superintendent) of the centre in advance and 
ascertain from him the date fixed for the practical. If any candidate fails to contact the Principal in time and 
ascertain the date fixed for practical this office will not take up the responsibility in the matter . 

28. The Chief Superintendent may fix the date of cach practical. Much publicity may be given for 
the information of the candidates as regard to the date fixed for practical examination . 

29 . Candidates who have failed only in practical examination and now appear for practicals should 
apply for admission to the examination in the prescribed form . 

30 . Candidates appearing both for the written and practical examination should produce their admission 
tickets to the examiner for identification , on all days of the examination . 
31 . 

Rules for the reappearance of the examination for betterment of results. 
" A candidate who passed the Examination (Final Year Diploma Examination in Engineering and 
Technology) will be given the option to appear again for the same Diploma Examination in Engineering and 
Technology as a full course candidate for betterment of result within a period of one year from the date of passing 
the Final Year Examination . But no candidate shall be permitted for such a reappearance for the betterment i 
result more than once" . Such candidate need not surrender the Diploma already issued . If any candidate 
submits application to appear for the examination as per the above rules, a declaration of the candidate ag 
mentioned below duly countersigned by the Head of the Institution should also be forwarded along with his 
application .

33. Admission tickets for the candidate will be issued by the Chief Superintendent of the Centre con . 
cemed at least five days before the commencement of the Examination . 

34. The Time- table for the written Examination will be published in Examination Centres, and in the 
Government Gazette in due course. 

35. Preparation of ' A' and ' B' lists.-- (a ) Separate 'A ' and 'B ' lists may be prepared in the case of candidates 
appearing for the First, Second and Final Year Diploma Examination in Engineering / Technology for each branch . 
Separate formsmay be used in the case of candidates appearing for the Examination simultaneously, and betterment 
of Result Separate forms will be supplied from this office. 

(b ) (i) . A'and ' B ' lists for Old Scheme candidates should be prepared in the form prescribed 
in the Old Scheme Examination . 

(ii) In the 'A ' and Blists the subject in which the candidate has yet to pass should be 
scored off and the name of equivalent subject should be entered in its place . 

(iii) Separate ' A ' and 'B ' lists may be prepared for each candidate appearing under the 
old scheme . However if more than one candidate is appearing for the same subject or subjects their names 
can be entered in the same sheet. 

(c) The previous Register Numbers of the tandidates should be noted in the A and B lists . 

(a) The B ' list of all candidates should also be prepared by the Head of the Institution 
and the same signed by the Principal under the seal of his Institution . The last date for the receipt of applications 
and nominal list in this office may be strictly adhered to . 

36. The Head of Institutions are requested to go through the rules and instructions contained in the 
notification for their guidance.

ഇൻറർവ്യൂ ഉണ്ടായിരിക്കുന്നതല്ല . തിരഞ്ഞെടുക്കപ്പെടുന്ന അപക്ഷകരെ യഥാസമയം സ്ക്കുളും ( പരവശന 
തീയതിയും അറിയിക്കുന്നതാണ്. അവർ നിലവിലുളള ചട്ടങ്ങൾ അനുസരിച്ച്ട്യൂഷൻഫീസ്മുതലായവ ഒടുക്കി 
സ്കൂളിൽചേർന്നുകൊളളണ്ടതാണ്. 

ഇതു സംബന്ധിച്ചുളള എല്ലാ വിവരങ്ങളും ഒടയിനിംഗ് സ്കൂളുകളുടെ പേരുകളും മറ്റും ഏതെങ്കിലും 
ജില്ലാ വിദ്യാഭ്യാസ ഓഫീസിലോ വിദ്യാഭ്യാസ ഡെ ഡ്യൂട്ടി ഡയറക്ടർ ആഫീസിലോ നേരിട്ട് അന്വേഷിച്ച് അറി ഞ്ഞ 
കൊണ്ടതാണ്.

Applications in the form prescribed in the Appendix to this notification are invited from qualified Keralites 
for selection to the Language Teachers ' Training course in Malayalam , Tamil, Sanskrit, Arabic , Kannada and 
Urdu at the various Language Teachers Training centres during 1985-86 . 

Candidates with the following qualifications are eligible for selection to the" Language Teachers Training 


course . 


--- 


1 


Title in Oriental Learning awarded by the Universities in Kerala for Malayalam For Tamil, Sanskrit, 
Kannada, Urdu and Arabic , a Title of Oriental learning in the concerned Language awarded or recognised by the 
Universities in Kerala . 

2 % of the Seats is reserved for physically handicapped persons. Age limit for admission to the course will 
be as follows: 

1. Candidates below the age of 17 years or above the age of 33 years as on 1-1-1985 are not eligible for 
admission to the course. 

2. Candidates belonging to other Backward Classes are allowed relaxation of 3 years in the Upper age limit 
and 5 years in the case of SC /ST. The upper age limit is also relaxable to the extent of approved teaching service. 
or service in the Defence Forces. 

et Each applicant has to remit an application fee for Rs. 5 undes the head of Account " 077 Education ( c ) 
Special Education (b ) other receipt (3 ) other items" . 

Candidates belonging to scheduled castes and scheduled tribes are exempted from payment of the 
application fee: 

Documents to be produced along with the applications are the following: 

1. Original chalan receipt for the remittance of the application fee of Rs. 5 . 
2. Copy of Certificate /Diploma of the Oriental Title Examination passed . 
3. Copy of theMark list ofthe Oriental Title Examination passed . 
4 . Copy of S.S. L. C. (relevant page) to prove the date of birth and community . 

5. Copy of Nativity Certificate

(i) Gazetted Officer of Central or State Government. 

OR 
(ii ) Headmasters of Aided High School ( The name and designation of the attesting Authority should 

be clearly stated ) .

ssioner, in the absence of necessary entries regarding their community in the S.S.L.C. Book .

case the candidate has not passed the qualifying Examination from Institution in the Kerala or native place is not 
noted in the S.S.L.C. The certificate will be considered as valid only if the Village Officer / Tahsildar has clearly 
Certified that the candidate is a native of Kerala or a permanent resident of Kerala.. 

Dependents of Jawans (wives children and unmarried sisters fully dependent on the Jawan ) should enclose a 
certificate obtained from the Local Tahsildar showing the relationship with the Jawan . The certificate should 
clearly state whether the candidate is fully dependent on the Jawans or not. Certificate obtained from any other 
persons will not be treated as valid for the purpose : 

Those who are eligible to get concession allowable to the physically handicapped person should produce 
certificate from a Medical Officer not below the rank of an Assistant Surgeon stating the nature of defect.

Applications in the form appended (Appendix ) are invited from natives of Kerala for selection to Hind 
Teacher's Training Course 1985-86 (open quota) . 

Candidates with the following qualifications are eligible for sclection , to the Hindi Teachers Training 
Course, 

(a): A title of Oriental learning in Hindi awarded or recognised by the Universities in Kerala 
(b ), Praveen of the Dekshina Bharat Hindi Prachar Sabha , Madras with a pass in the S.S.L.C. 

Examination conducted by thc Commissioner for Government Examinations, Kerala or its 

equivalent. 
(c ) Sahityacharya of Kerala, Hindi Prachar Sabha with a pass in S. S. L. C. Examination 

conducted by the Commissioner for Government Examinations, Kerala or its equivalent. 
Age limits :--Candidates must have attained the age of 17 years as on l-1-1985 and must not be above 
the age of 33 years as on 1-1-1985 , Candidates who belong to Scheduled Castes and Tribes are entitled to get a 
relaxation of 5 years in the upper age limits and candidates belonging to O.B.C. are eligible to get relaxation of 
3 years in the upper age limit. The upper age limit is also relaxable to the extent of approved teaching 
service or service in Defence Forces. In the case of Ex -servicemen , Certificates from Local" Tahsildar should 
also be produced 

2 % of seats is reserved for Physically handicapped persons. 

The envelopes containing applications should be superscribed " Application for selection to the Hindi 
Teachers Training Course 1985-86 " . 

Intending candidates should remit an application fee of Rs. 5 under the Head of Account " 077 Edn . 
C. Special Education (b ) other receipts 3 other items" . 

Candidates belonging to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled . Tribes are exempted from payment of 
application fee. 

All entries in the application form and its Annexure should be neatly written . No column should be 
left blank. If there are no particulars to be filled in the word "Nil may be written . 

The following documents must accompany the application : 

(i) Chalan receipt in original of the remittance of the application fee. 
(ii) A certificate in the form furnished below to prove Hindi Language qualification . ( This certificate 

should be from a High School Hindi Teacher in service and countersigned by the Headmaster

GENERAL INSTRUCTIONS TO THE CANDIDATE 


1. The application should reach the Director of Public Instruction , Trivandrum - 14 not later than 
30-3-1985, 5.00 p.m. Applications received after the due date will not be considered even if the remittance of 
application fee is made before the due date . So also defective applications will not be entertained . 

2. The candidates are requested to produce attested copy of the Community Certificate issued by the Local 
Village Oficer/Tahsildar/Deputy Tahsildar/Municipal Commissioner in the absence of necessary entries in the 
S.S.L.C. Book . Copy should be attested by a Gazetted Officer/Headmaster of aided school. Nameand designation 
of the attesting authority should be clearly furnished below the signature, Self attested copies of documents / 
certificateswill not be accepted . 

Those who are eligible to get the concession to the physically handicapped person should produce a certificate 
from a Medical Officer not below the rank of an Assistant Surgeon , stating the nature of defects. 

Original documents, copies ofwhich are attached to the application should be produced at the timeof 
admission to the Training Course. 

3. Dependents of Jawan (wife, children and unmarried sisters fully dependent on the Tawan ) should 
produce a certificate issued by the Local Tahsildar showing the relationship with the Jawan . Certificates obtained 
from any other persons will not be considered as valid . Copy of certificate should be attested by a Gazetted Officer / 
Headmaster of aided school. 

4. To ensure correct and safe handling of the documents attached to the application, candidates are 
advised to stitch the application form along with all the enclosure with thread at the left hand top comer. 

5. It must be clearly noted that appearing for the competitive test docs not give the candidates any 
guarantee that they will be selected for training . If later, it is found that the details furnished by a candidate 
are not correct and he/she is not in possession of requisite qualification, the Director of Public Instruction reserved 
the right to cancel his/her selection . The decision of the Director of Public Instruction as to the eligibility or 
otherwise of a candidate for selection will be final. 

The Director of Public Instruction will not enter into correspondence with any individual or organisation in 
respect of any matter concerned with the selection of candidates for training . 

Selection for Training Course will not guarantee employment after training.

ദർഘാസ പ്രമാണങ്ങളും മറന്നു വിശദവിവരങ്ങളും താഴെ ഒപ്പുവച്ച ഉദ്യോഗസ്ഥൻറ കാര്യാലയത്തിൽനിന്നും 
15-2-1985 മുതൽ എല്ലാ പ്രവൃത്തി ദിവസങ്ങളിലും പ്രവർ ത്തി സമയങ്ങളിലും ദർഘാസ് തീയതി ഉച്ചയ്ക്ക് 
1 മ ണിവരെയും ദർഘാസ് പ്രമാണത്തിനും വില രൊക്കം പണമായാമണിഒാർഡറായോ അടച്ച് & ഖാമൂലംഅപേ 
ക്ഷിച്ചാൽ ലഭിക്കുന്നതാണ്, ദർഘാസ് പ്രമാണത്തിനുവേണ്ടി അടച്ച തുക യാതൊരു കാരണവശാലും തിരികെ 
ലഭിക്കുന്നതല്ല . ദർഘാസ് ( പമാണങ്ങൾ പൊതുമരാമത്തുവകുപ്പിലെ അംഗീകത കരാറുകാർക്ക്മാത്രം ലഭിക്കുന്നതും 

അന്യോന്യം കൈമാറുവാൻ പാടില്ലാത്തതുമാകുന്നു . 

എക്സിക്യൂട്ടീവ് എഞ്ചിനീയ റെ അധികാരപ്പെടുത്തിയതും ( പവർത്തിയുടെ പേര് വ്യക്തമായി രേഖപ്പെടു 
ത്തിയതും ആവശ്യമായ സ്ററാമ്പ് പതിച്ച് . ഒപ്പിട്ടതുമായ നിരതവ്യംഅടച്ച രസീത് ദർഘാസിനോടൊപ്പം സമർപ്പി 
ക ണ്ടതാണ്. കേരള പൊതുമരാമത്ത് വകുപ്പിൽ നിലവിലുളള ദർഘാസിനെ സംബന്ധിച്ചുളള മറെറല്ലാ വ്യവ 
സ്ഥകളും ഈ ദർഘാസിനും ബാധകമായിരിക്കും.

Kerala Gazette No. 7 dated 12th February, 1985 , 
PART IV . 

Proceedings of the Director of Sociat Welfare, Trivandrum 
Sub :- Social Welfare Department--- Establishment--Final Gradation list of Ministerial Subordinate Service stafi 

as on 9-9-1975 — Published .. 
Read : 1. G. O. ( P ). No. 223 /75/LA & SWD dated 9-9-1975 . 

2. Order No. EF1-39517/80 ( A ) dated 18-2-1981 of the Director of Social Welfare, Trivandrum . 
ORDER No. EF1-1976 /84 /DSW . 

17th April 1984 . 
In the G. O. read first 

paper above , 

orders were issued for the creation of a new Department by name 
" Social Welfare Department” bringing all the then existing Social Welfare Schemes/Institutions with all 
personnel and perquisites) under the Special Officer , Special Nutrition Programme and those Social Welfare 
Institutions under he control of Inspector General of Prisons and the Probation Service attached to Jails 
Department. Therefore a fresh integrated seniority of such ministerial officers is to be prepared with reference to 
their service conditions as on 9-9-1975 . 

2. On verification ofG. O.Ms. 272 /77 / LA & SWD dated 26-9-1977 in which staff strength according to 
the ratio 1 : 2 was fixed for the first time in the Department it is seen that in the office of the Special Officer, 
Special Nutrition Programme and in the Vocational Training Centre, Kozhikode and in the Special Employment 
Bureau , Trivandrum , which were 

under the control ofthe Special Officer there were 5 sanctioned posts 
of U. D. Clerks and 7 posts of L. D. Clerks and they were maintained without fixing the ratio of 1 : 2. Further in 
the report leading to the G. O. of fixation of cadre strength 2 L. D. posts which were actually transferred in 1979 
from the Jails Department (though the 2 posts were ordered to be transferred to the SocialWelfare Department 
on 9-9-1915 vide also the G.O. read first paper above) were also taken into account in calculating the total 
number of 5 U. D. Clerks and 18 L. D. Clerks from the probation wing of Jails Department against actual posts of 
5 U. D - Clerks and 16 L. D. Clerks. On re -calculation and re -fixation of staff strength it is seen that in the 
Special Officer's office as on 8-9-1975 (ie. prior to the formation of the Department) that office is eligible for 
4 U. D. Clersand 8 L. D. Clerks instead of 5 U. D. Clerks and 7 L. D. Clerks. Along with this the 5 posts of 
U. D. Clerks and 16 L. D. Clerks posts actually transferred to the new Department from the Jails Department are 
added ( 12 + 21 = 33) and according to the ratio 1 : 2 11 U. D. Clerks and 22 L. D. Clerks are fixed . The 
11 U. D. Clerks are apportioned among those 3 in the office of the Special Officer and one deputationist in the 
post of Accountant cum -Store Keeper and the rest 7 among from the probation wing according to their dates of 
entry in the grade. On final analysis of all relevant aspects it is found that one U. D. Clerk in the office of the 
Special Officer will get promotion only on 7-1-1975 A. N. and that the vacancy assigned to Smt. K. Kunjulekshmi 
cn 1-1-1973 was not a substanjive 

vacancy . It is also seen that according to the options exercised finally, 
6 U. D. Clerks from the probation wing were transferred against 5 posts and the re-fixation benefit is to be given to 
the senior 

most 

regular L. D. Clerk with test qualifications in the integrated seniority list and also to 
Sri M. Vasudevan who was already - junior most U. D. Clerk from the probation wing and who enjoys the 
benefit of test exemption . 

3. Before finalising the list the claims of Smt. K. Kunjulekshmi and Sri P. V. Vasudevan Pillai (died in 
harness) for the vacancy of U. D. Clerk on 7-1-1975 A. N. caused by the reversion of Sri P. V. Abraham ta 
Harijan Welfare Department on expiry of his 2 years deputation term , have been examine in detail. Though 
both were regularised as L. D. Clerk on 1-11-1972 as per.G. O. Rt. 187/76 LA & SWD dated 23-1-1976 during 
the period of 2 years probation in the L. D. cadre from 1-11-1972. Smt. K. Kunjulekshmy took maternity leave 
for 3 months which is regularised . Sri P. V. Vasudevan Pillai did take only for 85 days Half pay leave during his 
probation period . Hence Sri P. V. Vasudevan Pillai completed his satisfactory period of probation earlier than 
that of Smt. K. Kunjulekshmy and as an approved probationer preference is given to Sri P. V. Vasudevan Pillai 
for filling up the regular vacancy. Both were test qualified at the time of occurrence of vacancy as on 7-1-1975 A.N. 

4. On refixation of the cadre strength of L. D. Clerks and U. D. Clerks as on 9-9-1975 it is already scen 
that there are 7 U.D. posts due to the officers from the Jails Department. Accordingly Sri M. Vasudevan , 
U. D. Clerk has been given the sixth vacancy from the Jails Department and Smt. P. Sulochana the senior most 
qualified regular L. D. Clerk is given the 7th vacancy . 
* 5. According to the 

date of effective advice (if there is such an advice in the L. D. Cadre ) of the 
P.S. C. seniority of officers in the L. D. Cadre has been fixed . In the absence of certain officers such a date 
seniority has been reckoned from the date of entry in the grade. In the promoted U. D. cadre date of 
commencement of continuous service is reckoned for seniority . The seniority in the provisional service in higher 
categories after 9-9-1975 is liable to be changed . 

6. There is difference between the preliminary tentative list and this final list in regard to test qualification , 
In the final list if any officer had no test completed qualification as on 9-9-1975 such a one is not noted against his 
whereas in the 

list 

tentative the position noted in the 
name 

Service 

Book as such was transcribed. 
Sri M. Vasudevan, 

eventhough he did not complete Account Test Lower as on 9-9-1975 , is entitled to be 
regularised from 1-12-1972 as per G , O.Ms. 22 /76/ PD dated 19-1-1976 [he completed the test Account Test (Lower) 
on 15-4-1976 ) and hence he is included in the list of regular U. D. Clerk . 
7 . The list is finalised and will be published in the Gazette for inforniation of all concerned .

NOTIFICATION 

18th January 1985 . 
The Cochin Devaswom Board caused to enquire 
about the proposal of the Cochin Thirumala 
Devaswom ommitte for the sale of 3 Acres of wet 
land and the Board have satisfied that in the interest 
of the Devaswom , the sale of the property is 
advantageous to the Devaswom . Therefore in 
exercise of the powers conferred in Section 86 ( 1) of 
the Travancore Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions 
Act XV of 1950 , the Cochin Devaswom Board hereby 
pleased to sanction and approve the sale of 3 Acres of 
wet land in Sy . No. 486/1 of Nadama Village 
belonging to Cochin Thirumala Devaswom to 
Sri . B. Ř . Ajith for a sum not less than Rs 1,35,000 .

NOTIFICATION 
1. The annual subscription to the Kerala State Government Gazette falls duc on the 1st January or Ist 
July of every year and should be paid in advance on or before 10th of December or 10th of June every year so 
ay to supply the Gazette from 1st January or Ist July as the case may be . 

2. Subscription will not be accepted for an uneven calendar full year or half year or for a shorter 
period less than half year. 

3. Subscription for full Gazette, Part I, Part IA Part IB , Part II, Part IV , and Departmental sheets 
in Part III, can be paid half-yearly and annually . 

4 . Payments of subscription may be made either by cash or postal money order or original Treasury 
Chalan . Postage stamps will not be accepted . Cheques and Demand Drafts also will not be accepter 

5. Money order without full instructions relating to the period of subscription or the name of the 
Part of the departmental sheets for which subscription is paid , 

wili 

not be normally accepted and even if 
accepted the supply of the Gazette will 

commence only on the receipt of the relevant details . 
6. Läte subscription also will be accepted . In such cases back issues of the Gazette will 110t be supplicd .

can be paid at any, time of the year but will be credited to account only for the year beginning

late the subscribers should specify the period for which the subscription is intended

be considered

Bame of the 

District in which the Post Office is situate should be included in the address in order to ensure 
prompt supply of Gazette to subscribers.
